# Notion integration (`pyrunner_integrations.notion`)

Notion for scripts: query databases, create and update pages, append blocks and search.

Functions take Notion's ids (a page's or database's id, with or without the
dashes; it is the last part of its URL) and return Notion's own objects:
pages with their `properties`, blocks, databases. Page properties are
written in Notion's shape, for example a database row:

```python
{"Name": {"title": [{"text": {"content": "Ada"}}]},
 "Status": {"select": {"name": "New"}},
 "Score": {"number": 9}}
```

Where a function takes blocks, a plain string is a paragraph, so
`notion.append_blocks(page_id, ["First line", "Second line"])` works. Lists come
page by page as you read them; `limit` stops early.

The connection is a Notion integration: an OAuth connection, or an internal
integration's secret pasted as its access token. It only sees the pages and
databases shared with it in Notion. Calls use Notion API version 2022-06-28
(the connection sends it).

## Connection

It uses a connection of the **Notion** kind (provider `notion`), which signs in with OAuth (Connect or a pasted token). Add one under **Connections** in the sidebar and grant it to the script. Every function takes `connection=`: the connection's name, or nothing for the script's one `notion` connection.

The credentials go only to the connection's base URL; a redirect elsewhere goes on without them.

## Example

```python
from pyrunner_integrations import notion

TASKS = "0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef"   # the database's id: the end of its URL

# Every open task, soonest first.
for page in notion.query_database(TASKS, filter={"property": "Status", "select": {"equals": "Open"}},
                                  sorts=[{"property": "Due", "direction": "ascending"}]):
    print(page["properties"]["Name"]["title"][0]["plain_text"])

# A new row, with a note in its page.
page = notion.create_page(database_id=TASKS, title="Call Ada",
                          properties={"Status": {"select": {"name": "Open"}}})
notion.append_blocks(page["id"], ["Ask about the invoice."])

# Later: mark it done.
notion.update_page(page["id"], {"Status": {"select": {"name": "Done"}}})
```

## Functions

### query_database

```python
notion.query_database(database_id, *, filter=None, sorts=None, limit=None, connection=None)
```

Yield the database's pages (its rows) that match `filter`, fetching pages as it goes.

`filter` and `sorts` are Notion's query objects. `limit` stops after
that many. For example:

```python
open_tasks = notion.query_database(
    database_id,
    filter={"property": "Status", "select": {"equals": "Open"}},
    sorts=[{"property": "Due", "direction": "ascending"}],
)
for page in open_tasks:
    print(page["id"], page["properties"]["Name"]["title"][0]["plain_text"])
```

### get_database

```python
notion.get_database(database_id, *, connection=None)
```

The database itself: its `title` and its `properties` (the columns, with their types and options).

For example:

```python
columns = notion.get_database(database_id)["properties"]
```

### get_page

```python
notion.get_page(page_id, *, connection=None)
```

One page with its `properties` (its content is in `list_blocks(page_id)`).

For example:

```python
page = notion.get_page(page_id)
print(page["url"])
```

### create_page

```python
notion.create_page(*, database_id=None, page_id=None, properties=None, title=None, children=None, connection=None)
```

Create a page in a database (a new row) or under a page, and return it.

Give `database_id` or `page_id`. `properties` are the new page's
values; `title` sets its title (the database's title column, whatever its
name). `children` are its content blocks (strings are paragraphs); past
Notion's 100 per request the rest is appended after it is created. For example:

```python
page = notion.create_page(
    database_id=database_id,
    title="Call Ada",
    properties={"Status": {"select": {"name": "Open"}}},
    children=["Ask about the invoice."],
)
```

### update_page

```python
notion.update_page(page_id, properties=None, *, title=None, archived=None, connection=None)
```

Change a page's `properties` (only those given) and return it.

`title` sets its title; `archived=True` moves it to the trash
(`False` restores it). For example:

```python
notion.update_page(page_id, {"Status": {"select": {"name": "Done"}}})
```

### append_blocks

```python
notion.append_blocks(block_id, blocks, *, connection=None)
```

Add `blocks` at the end of a page (or of a block that holds others); returns the new blocks.

`blocks` is a list, or one block. Strings are paragraphs; other blocks
are Notion block objects. More than 100 go in several requests. For example:

```python
notion.append_blocks(page_id, [
    {"type": "heading_2", "heading_2": {"rich_text": [{"text": {"content": "Summary"}}]}},
    "Everything went fine.",
])
```

### list_blocks

```python
notion.list_blocks(block_id, *, limit=None, connection=None)
```

Yield a page's content blocks (or a block's children), in order, fetching pages as it goes.

Only the first level: a block with `has_children` holds more, read them
with `list_blocks(block["id"])`. For example:

```python
for block in notion.list_blocks(page_id):
    if block["type"] == "paragraph":
        print("".join(t["plain_text"] for t in block["paragraph"]["rich_text"]))
```

### search

```python
notion.search(query='', *, kind=None, limit=None, connection=None)
```

Yield the pages and databases shared with the integration whose title matches `query`.

`kind="page"` or `kind="database"` keeps only those. An empty query
lists everything shared. For example:

```python
for result in notion.search("Roadmap", kind="database", limit=5):
    print(result["id"])
```

### client

```python
notion.client(connection=None, *, timeout=30)
```

The shared client of `connection`, for calls this module has no function for.

Paths are relative to `https://api.notion.com`. For example:

```python
user = notion.client().get("/v1/users/me")
```

## Errors

Every function raises `pyrunner_integrations.IntegrationError` (a `pyrunner_connections.ConnectionsError`, so one `except` catches both) with `code`, `status` (the HTTP status, or None) and `retry_after` (seconds, or None). Its message never holds the connection's credentials. Before raising, the client retries a 429 (or a 503 with Retry-After) up to 3 times, waiting what the service asks (up to 60 s; longer, and the error says it in `retry_after`) or else 1, 2 or 4 seconds; other 5xx replies and lost connections only for GET, PUT, DELETE and other calls that are safe to repeat. After a 401 it asks PyRun once for new credentials (an OAuth token is refreshed then) and tries again.

| Code | When |
|---|---|
| `INVALID_REQUEST` | The service refused the request as malformed (HTTP 400, 405 or 422). |
| `UNAUTHORIZED` | The service refused the credentials (HTTP 401), also after PyRun was asked for new ones. |
| `FORBIDDEN` | The account may not do this (HTTP 403): a missing scope or permission. |
| `NOT_FOUND` | No such thing (HTTP 404 or 410). |
| `CONFLICT` | It clashes with the current state (HTTP 409 or 412). |
| `RATE_LIMITED` | Too many requests (HTTP 429), still after the retries; `retry_after` says when to try again. |
| `HTTP_ERROR` | Any other 4xx reply. |
| `SERVER_ERROR` | The service failed (HTTP 5xx), still after the retries. |
| `UNREACHABLE` | The service couldn't be reached (DNS, refused connection, TLS). |
| `TIMEOUT` | No reply in time. |
| `BAD_RESPONSE` | A reply that can't be used: broken JSON, too many redirects or pages, a repeated page cursor. |
| `NOT_HTTP` | The connection isn't an HTTP connection (an SMTP login). |
| `CONNECTION_...` | The connection can't be used: `CONNECTION_NOT_FOUND`, `CONNECTION_EXPIRED`... (see [Connections](../run-context.md#connections)). |
